$comment: The performance budgets (#22), in one place: e2e/budgets.ts judges measurements against them and CI fails a run that misses one. Timings are judged on the MEDIAN of several samples against `budget`, and the 95th percentile against `budget` times `noise` (a slow sample on a busy CI runner must not fail the build; a regression that slows every other sample does). Sizes and counts are exact and have no noise; a share of the CPU is a timing. A later issue adds its own entry here and judges it with `expectWithinBudget` (e2e/budgets.ts).

coldStart.what: From starting the app's process to the shell being in the page with the backend answering (the `app-usable` mark)

screenSwitch.what: From a click on a navigation link to the first frame with the screen in it (a screen that was shown before)

initialJs.what: The JavaScript the page loads before anything else: index.html's module script and its modulepreloads, uncompressed (the app reads them from disk, so the size is parse time)

longTask.what: The longest task on the page's main thread while the Flight data screen shows a vehicle's telemetry (25 Hz), after it settled

paletteOpen.what: From Ctrl+P to the first frame with the palette's search box focused, with 1,500 parameters loaded

paletteKeystroke.what: From a keystroke in the palette to its rows being in the page (the next task), with 1,500 parameters loaded

telemetryUpdates.what: The telemetry updates the page gets in a second (each one is a render), while the vehicle sends at 50 Hz (#26): the backend coalesces them. A count, so no noise

telemetryIdleCpu.what: The share of a second the page's main thread is busy (DevTools' TaskDuration) on the Flight data screen, idle, while the vehicle sends at 50 Hz (#26)

tableScroll.what: The table's own work for a scroll step: from the scroll to its rows drawn and laid out (before the paint), while the Plan table, at the plan's 1,000 items (its most), is scrolled a few rows at a time. Within a 60 fps frame (16.7 ms) with room left for the paint in the median
